newsitem.title: USA: Worldcom profits fall after MFS merger charge.
newsitem.headline: Worldcom profits fall after MFS merger charge.

text.p: WorldCom Inc. said Wednesday its net income fell in the first quarter as the telecommunications provider took a $84 million charge to pay for its merger with MFS Communications Co. Inc.

Profits fell to $49.7 million, or 5 cents a share, in the quarter from $86.3 million, or 21 cents a share, in the year-ago period. The latest results take into account $84 million in costs related to the merger with MFS on Dec. 31.
Operating income slid to $171 million from $196 million.
Revenues soared 62 percent to $1.68 billion from $1.03 billion, boosted by the merger with MFS as well as strong internal growth across all communications services.
Long distance traffic jumped 52 percent over the previous year.

"Our strong results clearly underscore the importance of the recent merger with MFS and highlight the value of being a full service, facilities-based communications provider," said Bernard Ebbers, president and chief executive of WorldCom.

WorldCom said revenues from its UUNET Technologies, Inc. subsidiary, the world's largest provider of Internet services, soared 185 percent to $111 million in the first quarter from $39 million in the year-ago period.
Revenues from other operations, including MFS Network Technologies, operator services, broadcast operations and other equipment and software sales, rose 21 percent to $98 million from $81 million.
WorldCom, based in Jackson, Miss., operates in more than 50 countries, providing local, long distance, international and Internet services.
The company's stock rose 50 cents to $23.25 on Nasdaq in early afternoon trading.
